solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Job-seeker apparently in charge in factory

parts.note: AP is a dictionary abbreviation for apparently

indicators.note: the second in places the in-charge letters inside the factory word

parts.note: a plant is a factory or works
IC, written I/C, is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Someone after a job appears to be running the factory already.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue has two 'in's: the first is part of the phrase 'in charge', and only the second works as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate who puts in a formal request for a post is someone seeking work.

clue.text: Attack American president

parts.note: Bush is the surname of two US presidents

explanation.surface: A US head of state is accused of launching an assault.
explanation.definitionFit: An ambush is a surprise attack from hiding, so the noun is an exact synonym.

clue.text: Dolly knocked back gin before appearing

indicators.note: to knock back a drink suggests the word for gin is turned backwards here

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for catching animals
on means appearing, as a performer is on stage

explanation.surface: Dolly downed a gin before going out to perform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knocked back' looks like drinking, and 'gin' like the spirit, but gin here is the animal snare.
explanation.definitionFit: Dolly Parton is the American country singer, so her first name stands for her surname by example.

clue.text: Old warriors rising up in part of London

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: EC1 is a London postal district, with the 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Ancient fighters are staging an uprising in a corner of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: EC1 is a postcode district in central London; its digit 1 serves as the letter I, and 'rising up' turns IN EC1 upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: The tribe of Boudicca, which fought the Romans in ancient Britain, was a warlike people of antiquity.

clue.text: Like version of nine-hole golf at Sandwich to begin with

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworked form, so these letters are rearranged
to begin with points to just the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A short round of golf at the Kent links of Sandwich is described.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich, a Kent town, hosts Royal St George's, an Open Championship golf course; the anagram of NINEHOLEGOLFAT plus its first letter S gives the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Something along those lines is similar to it, so the phrase works as a synonym for the preposition meaning similar to.

clue.text: Get upset about suffering right shower during preparation for the classroom

indicators.note: about means going round, so the turned word encloses the rest
in a down clue, upset turns the word upside down, so it reads from the bottom

parts.note: an ache is a kind of suffering
a shower is a brief fall of rain
during means in, as in the course of

explanation.surface: Someone gets cross about getting soaked in a downpour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upset' reverses the first word, read upwards in a down clue, and 'about' wraps it round the four pieces that follow; 'shower' is rain, not a bathroom fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Courses that train future schoolteachers are exactly what readies someone to teach a class.

clue.text: Very loudly talk about places to live

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for talk goes around the musical letters

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
FF, fortissimo, is the musical direction for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone talks very loudly about where people live.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaff is British slang for a home or house, so the plural is homes.

clue.text: Fine fellow having party over in Hants town

indicators.note: in places the turned party inside the town's name

parts.note: Gosport is a town in Hampshire (Hants), on Portsmouth Harbour

indicators.note: over means the word is turned round

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A decent chap is throwing a party in a Hampshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: Hants is the short form of Hampshire, an English county on the south coast; 'over' reverses the party word.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who accepts defeat or teasing cheerfully is called that, so it means a decent, agreeable person.

clue.text: Bird depicted in a sort of porcelain found in Florence

indicators.note: found in places the porcelain words inside the shortened name

parts.note: Flo is the short form of the name Florence
Ming is fine Chinese porcelain from the Ming dynasty

explanation.surface: A bird is painted on a Chinese vase discovered in the Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Florence' looks like the city in Italy but is the girl's name, cut to FLO.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink wading bird with long legs is one particular species of bird.

clue.text: South-Eastern woven, silky material

indicators.note: woven means the letters are interlaced into a new arrangement, like threads

explanation.surface: A silky fabric woven in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarsenet is a fine, soft silk fabric used chiefly for linings.

clue.text: An expression of great joy, with seafood making comeback in Mediterranean location

indicators.note: making a comeback means the whole run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: ole is the Spanish cry of delight heard at bullfights
crab is a shellfish eaten as seafood

explanation.surface: Someone shouts with delight over a seafood dish on the Spanish coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making comeback' sits by the seafood but reverses all three pieces together, the article and the cry included.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan city stands on the Mediterranean coast of Spain, so it is an example of a place there.

clue.text: During revolution, group of Syrian officers broadcasting

indicators.note: during a revolution things are turned round, so the run of letters is read backwards
group of means a run of consecutive letters taken from the two words

explanation.surface: A clique of Syrian army officers seizes the radio station during a coup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'During revolution' looks like scene-setting for a coup, but it signals the reversal of the letters taken from 'Syrian officers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme going out live on radio or television is said to be transmitting in that state.

clue.text: Composing music for recording

definitions.meaning: writing the score for a film or play
keeping a tally of points in a game

explanation.surface: A composer writes music for a studio session.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both writing the music for a production and noting down points in a match.

clue.text: House with steps opposite?

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: A house stands across the way from a set of steps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opposite' looks like a position across the road, but here it is the attitude of being opposed; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone antagonistic is set against you, so the adjective for opposing fits with a hint of wordplay.

clue.text: Language test tough? René has gone wrong

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for vehicles in Britain

indicators.note: gone wrong means these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: René has flunked a hard language exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the UK's yearly roadworthiness check on cars, named after the old Ministry of Transport; 'has gone wrong' scrambles the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's native language, the first one learnt as a child, is what this phrase names.

clue.text: Administrative expert or a singer, in a way

indicators.note: in a way suggests the letters are taken in some other fashion, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A capable administrator, or perhaps a vocalist of sorts.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone skilled at arranging events and logistics is a person expert in administration.

clue.text: Rifles convict concealed in great quantities

indicators.note: concealed in places the convict inside the word for great quantities

parts.note: piles of something are large amounts
a lag, or old lag, is slang for a prisoner

explanation.surface: Guns are smuggled by a prisoner hidden among stacks of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifles' looks like a noun for guns, but it is the verb meaning ransacks.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and rob it, which is what plundering does.

clue.text: For one's pet project, pounds saved? Highly likely

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: saved means kept inside, so the money letter goes within the pet project

parts.note: a person's baby is the scheme they dote on
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Someone backs a favourite scheme and quite likely saves money by it.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means in all likelihood, the same strong expectation as the phrase.

clue.text: One unusual thing, holding back gun that's out of order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: holding means the word for unusual thing goes round the turned gun

parts.note: a rarity is something uncommon

indicators.note: back means the name of the gun is read in reverse

parts.note: a Luger is a German pistol

explanation.surface: A rare object conceals a firearm that is not quite above board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' reverses the pistol's name, and 'holding' sets it inside the unusual-thing word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An anomaly or breach of the rules is something not in proper sequence or order.

clue.text: Nirvana singer and half of band in the money

indicators.note: in places those letters inside the word for money

parts.note: coin is cash in metal form

indicators.note: half of takes just the first two of the word's four letters

explanation.surface: The rock star and some of his band are rolling in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like Nirvana itself, but only its first half, BA, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Kurt Cobain was the lead vocalist of the American grunge group Nirvana.

clue.text: Stick small plug in aforementioned place

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a plug for a product
here means the place just spoken of

explanation.surface: Someone fixes a small stopper in the spot already mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' looks like a stopper for a hole, but it is publicity.
explanation.definitionFit: To stick to something is to cling or remain attached, the same verb sense.

clue.text: Country outlaw held by Trotsky, say

indicators.note: held by places the outlaw word inside the first name

parts.note: Leon Trotsky was the Russian revolutionary, so Trotsky is an example of a Leon
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A criminal is captured by the Russian revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a noun for a bandit, but it is the verb meaning prohibit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern state on the Mediterranean is one particular nation.

clue.text: Trendy people sound self-satisfied, wearing topless dress

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the crow word is inside the trimmed dress word
topless means the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to dress a wound is to bind it
to crow is to boast smugly

explanation.surface: Fashionable folk sound smug while wearing revealing outfits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' looks like a garment, but it is the verb for bandaging, BIND, which 'topless' cuts to IND.
explanation.definitionFit: The fashionable, exclusive set of people who are in vogue is called by this phrase.

clue.text: Plebeian headgear put on monarch, for a lark

parts.note: a flat cloth cap is the working man's hat
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A common man's cap is put on the king's head as a joke.
explanation.definitionFit: A caper is a playful prank or escapade, the same as a bit of fun.

clue.text: Scoffs scrambled eggs for starters, along with giant turnover

indicators.note: turnover means the whole collection is flipped round and read backwards
for starters points to the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: giant means big

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down scrambled eggs as a first course, followed by a huge pastry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffs' looks like eating greedily, but it is jeers; 'turnover' looks like a pastry yet reverses SE and BIG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Taunting remarks are mocking words, and to scoff at someone is to jeer, the same verb sense.

clue.text: High-flier having trouble with map in Kent area?

indicators.note: in places the trouble and map words inside the area letters

parts.note: Kent is in the South East of England, abbreviated SE
to ail is to trouble
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: An ambitious person struggles with a map somewhere in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is an English county in the South East region, so it gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider, an engineless aircraft, literally flies high, a playful twist on the term for an achiever.

clue.text: Tom doesn't have weak voice?

indicators.note: doesn't have means one letter is removed from the name

parts.note: Tom Sawyer is Mark Twain's boy hero

explanation.surface: Tom lacks a feeble voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stretches: someone who says things is a voice in a debate; the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: One who utters words is a speaker, which is a voice in the sense of a person expressing views.

clue.text: Great fun! I act and I say little on stage

indicators.note: act here suggests putting on a performance, so the letters play new roles in a fresh order

explanation.surface: An actor in a bit part enjoys the fun of performing without many lines.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurante is a ballet dancer in the corps or an extra with no lines, so the role speaks little.
